title: Time to Set Sail
subtitle: A wave has come crashing down. Grab your umbrella and hold on to the railing.

trails.title: In the "Storm"
trails.description: No one is spared from the scourge of time, yet some still dare to try. How many years has Vertin been walking in the "Storm"?

content.text:
Sample Name: "Storm" Raindrop
Analyzed by: Laplace Scientific Computing Center
Sampling Date: [Obscured by liquid stain]/27 They asked a 12-year-old to collect samples?
Sample Quantity: 5 ml
Objective: Composition of "Storm" Raindrop
Analysis Results:
The sample contains water, sulfur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide, suspended solids (sediment particles, human hair, skin flakes, and dust), and unknown matter.
Further observation of the unknown matter through arcane imaging shows that the substance presents a bifurcated structure with radial energy fluctuations, identified as an unstable unknown nuclide (temporarily named "Asymmetrical Nuclide R"). The substance disappeared 5 seconds after observation. In the image captured in the 4th second, the dispersion of surrounding energy was observed. No stable state of Asymmetrical Nuclide R was observed.
A controlled experiment was conducted to explore the nature of Asymmetrical Nuclide R. Based on the results, it is believed that Asymmetrical Nuclide R is an important constituent in determining the characteristics of the "Storm." Further follow-up studies are recommended.

Appendix 1: Image of Asymmetrical Nuclide R
[A black and white photograph taken during the experiment, in the center of which a white luminous "γ"-shaped substance can be distinguished.]

Appendix 2: Experiment Recording #1
"For this direct contact experiment, 0.5 ml of raindrop was placed in contact with a laboratory mouse. Hair and skin tissue damage and deformation started from the contact site, with swelling observed around the wound. The wound spread outward ..."
"Final depth of the wound ... about 3 mm, diameter ... about 11.5 mm."

Appendix 3: Experiment Recording #2
"For this direct contact experiment, 0.5 ml of remaining raindrop was placed in contact with a laboratory mouse after the disappearance of Asymmetrical Nuclide R."
"No visible skin tissue damage, no wounds."
No one is spared from the scourge of time, yet some still dare to try. How many years has Vertin been walking in the "Storm"?
4 / Four years / four years / 4 year / 4 years / Four Years / four-year / ４

items.text: Time to Set Sail

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I will explain all of these as briefly as possible.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Good news.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: The analysis report on the mask you submitted to the Scientific Computing Center is now available, Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: We've found the same component in it as the raindrop from the Storm.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: This is a component named "asymmetrical nuclide R" by the Scientific Computing Center.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Its name comes from the bifurcation structure it presents under the arcanum imaging.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: The Scientific Computing Center has also run some tests on the samples of the raindrops you previously submitted. After removing all water, mud, human hair, and dandruff within, the remaining unanalyzable component is what we called "asymmetrical nuclide R."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What a familiar name.
Yes. As an expedient, she borrowed the first half of it to make up the answer to the "Three Questions."
Mesmer Jr. doesn't pay attention to her murmuring.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: But it disappeared right away, and we only have a photo of it.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Fortunately, we extracted the stable form of it from the Manus mask.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: It might be the key to staying immune to the "Storm."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Does that mean it'll be possible for the Scientific Computing Center to develop protective gears which are immune to the "Storm," like the Manus does?

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Seems to be so. A credit to you.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: The whole center is crazy about it, and I'm responsible for passing along the good news on behalf of my fatigued colleagues who stayed up all night and suffered from neurasthenia.
Mesmer passes them a heavy leather box.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: We need more samples.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: This is the sampling device for "asymmetrical nuclide R." It's the one and only. The manual is in the interlayer.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'll be careful. Thank you, Mesmer.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Don't be. I'm just delivering this for someone else.
This is the first time she has seen her since waking up.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: How do you feel now? I'm sorry about what happened in the rehab center.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I'm good. It just helped me further verify some factual information about arcanists.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: It's just ... I thought you weren't one of them, Vertin.
Mesmer adjusts her cufflinks and quickly walks away.
At the same time, the first assistant rushes from the other side of the corridor.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I just heard some spirit-lifting news at the hall. Phenomenal achievement, Timekeeper!
Sonetto's face brightens with sheer delight.
She has changed back into her familiar attire.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: It's a tremendous breakthrough in our fight with Manus Vindictae. Everyone at the headquarters is cheering.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Although I don't know what this component really is. Is it a kind of ritual or a unique substance?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That'll be the next thing to find out in our investigation, I think.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Manus Vindictae always has more information on the "Storm" and how to be immune to it. We've been trying our best to keep up with their progress.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Fortunately, now we have another direction.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Oh, and these are the files you asked me to search for.
Sonetto hands out a stack of magazines with yellowing covers, each corner carefully flattened.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Luckily, the SPDM library has every single issue of Global Arcane Geography since the 1960s.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Also, Ms. Sotheby accepted your request.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank you, Sonetto.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: With these files and the help of Regulus ... That should be enough.
The figures of the big names are moving between piles of paperwork ...
And someone is in big trouble.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Haha, yeah, go on, what else do you get except for playing dumb? You cunning flower-headed tin box!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Speak! Tell us what you know!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Like what were you doing in the Olitiau's base? In what way are you associated with Manus Vindictae? And who put you in that box which has Vertin's name on it?!
I, I have no idea.
The rockin' pirate advances while her hostage slowly retreats.
Till she knocks into someone more callous.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: And those ridiculous radio programs, end of the 20th century, Voice of the Millennium, and Roaming in Apeiron ...

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Don't waste our time. Otherwise, we have no choice but bathe you with this bottle of vodka.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Geez, do you really mean that? Anything less cruel?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Formalin, of course! I never waste my drinks.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Yeah, that's more like it!
The kidnappers smile grimly.
But I, I really don't know anything.
I'm just the receiver of signals. Please believe me!
When I woke up, I was already in that box!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: This interrogation won't get us anywhere.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Laplace didn't detect any unusual arcane marks on her.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: But she was there with those Manus pawns in that base!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Say anything you want, she will still be a solid suspect.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes, I understand what you mean. But for now, the evidence can't support our speculation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: A field trip may be helpful, I guess.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What's your plan? Will you come with me?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I've informed Madam Z. This will be the first official field mission of our team.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sotheby and Druvis are still on leave. They will not take part in this action.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: While Ms. Moissan will stay put in the Foundation's headquarters as our contact.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Wait, a field mission?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Didn't we just come back from that Olitiau base? Besides, where is this "field"?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The Apollo Star we just heard about means the sun. The Ford Sextant Model T is an arcane device produced in the early 19th century. The Scientific Computing Center has one of those as a part of their collection.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The Gorgon Current is mostly created in the Aegean Sea, near the Balkan Peninsula. I remembered an arcanum magazine in the 1970s had a detailed article about this and introduced the circulating current. I read it in the periodical room in SPDM.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The current will be flowing backwards every time the Earth is at aphelion and perihelion. This is also known as the Current Reversal.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Which is on the third day of January and July this year.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And the time in the outside world is ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: January 1st, 1914.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Are you saying that all those broadcasts are leading us to an actual place?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ah, why? I thought we'd have a nice break after this!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Regulus, you've been longing for a ship, haven't you?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What if I tell you that I have got you one?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Now, hold on a second.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Come to think of it, it wasn't the flower-headed radio thingy who tricked me into the Aegean Sea. It was ... Vertin?!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Watch out, the big waves!!!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: F**k! This is enough! Su-01ве!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Wait! Lilya, are you sure about taking off in such stormy weather?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: This isn't a normal storm. Something is attacking us from the ocean!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I need to pull it out! You guys go study that whatever instruction right now!
The red 38 rocket takes off and speeds across the sky like a shooting star.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Haha, I finally got you, d**n b*****d!

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: It's my turn!
TO BE CONTINUED…
